pr_title: fix: prevent dropping materialized views on Postgres versions < 9.3
pr_body:

### Description of change

<!--

  why this change is needed, and how you've verified that it
  corrects what you intended.

  In some cases it may be helpful to include the current behavior
  and the new behavior.

Materialized views introduced in Postgres 9.3. This PR adds version check before dropping materialized views to prevent errors on Postgres versions lower than 9.3

Fixes #7714

pr_comments:
However, I agree with the comment in the related issue:

> [Postgres 9.2](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/) official support was ended in 2017. We can't keep backward compatibility for all existing database versions.

It'd be easier to update the documentation to just say we require Postgres >= 9.3

issue_context.title: PostgreSQL - QueryFailedError: relation "pg_matviews" does not exist
issue_context.body:
## Issue Description
After updating from 0.2.32 to [0.2.33](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/compare/0.2.33...master)-[34](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/compare/0.2.34...master), the pg driver tries to select a non-existent relation "pg_matviews"

### Actual Behavior
```sh
query: START TRANSACTION
query: SELECT 'DROP VIEW IF EXISTS "' || schemaname || '"."' || viewname || '" CASCADE;' as "query" FROM "pg_views" WHERE "schemaname" IN (current_schema()) AND "viewname" NOT IN ('geography_columns', 'geometry_columns', 'raster_columns', 'raster_overviews')
query: SELECT 'DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS "' || schemaname || '"."' || matviewname || '" CASCADE;' as "query" FROM "pg_matviews" WHERE "schemaname" IN (current_schema())
query failed: SELECT 'DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS "' || schemaname || '"."' || matviewname || '" CASCADE;' as "query" FROM "pg_matviews" WHERE "schemaname" IN (current_schema())
error: error: relation "pg_matviews" does not exist
    at Parser.parseErrorMessage (/home/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:287:98)
    at Parser.handlePacket (/home/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:126:29)
    at Parser.parse (/home/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:39:38)
    at Socket.<anonymous> (/home/node_modules/pg-protocol/dist/index.js:11:42)
    at Socket.emit (events.js:376:20)
    at addChunk (internal/streams/readable.js:309:12)
    at readableAddChunk (internal/streams/readable.js:284:9)
    at Socket.Readable.push (internal/streams/readable.js:223:10)
    at TCP.onStreamRead (internal/stream_base_commons.js:188:23) {
  length: 103,
  severity: 'ERROR',
  code: '42P01',
  detail: undefined,
  hint: undefined,
  position: '115',
  internalPosition: undefined,
  internalQuery: undefined,
  where: undefined,
  schema: undefined,
  table: undefined,
  column: undefined,
  dataType: undefined,
  constraint: undefined,
  file: 'parse_relation.c',
  line: '874',
  routine: 'parserOpenTable'
}
query: ROLLBACK
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `npm i typeorm@0.2.33`
2. Create docker-compose.yaml
```yaml
version: '3.5'
services:
  postgres:
    image: mdillon/postgis:9.2-alpine
    ports:
      - '5432:5432'
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: database
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
```
3. Use this TypeORM options:
```json
{
  "name": "development",
  "type": "postgres",
  "host": "localhost",
  "port": 5432,
  "cache": true,
  "logging": "all",
  "database": "database",
  "username": "postgres",
  "password": "postgres",
  "dropSchema": true,
  "synchronize": true,
  "migrationsRun": true,
}
``` 

### My Environment
| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    |     Solus OS 4.2     |
| Node.js version     | 14.17.0 |
| Typescript version  | 4.3.2 |
| TypeORM version     | 0.2.23^ |
| PostGIS | 9.2 |

### Relevant Database Driver(s)
- [x] `postgres`

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?
- [x] No, I don't have the time, although I believe I could do it if I had the time...
comments: `pg_matviews` was added in `PostgreSQL 9.3`. You need to update your Postgres docker image to a newer version.
@AlexMesser, It seems to me that there should be backwards compatibility for other database versions
[Postgres 9.2](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/) official support was ended in 2017. We can't keep backward compatibility for all existing database versions.

@AlexMesser Maybe it's worth mentioning this in the documentation? It's just that many cloud providers support outdated Postgres versions, not to mention situations where it is possible to update the ORM, but there is no way to update the RDMS.
@H6LS1S what action leads to this error? Calling `connection.dropDatabase()` ?
should be fixed by #7716 in `0.2.35`. Please stick with `0.2.32` for now.

Will databases generally be supported past EOL? Seems like a consistent policy is better here. Better to focus on supporting current.

If the DB can't be upgraded then it's prolly a company and they can pay for support perhaps

review_comments: Wouldn't it be better if `getVersion` moved to **PostgresDriver**, also cache the result as a property in the driver (ex: `serverVersion`) that could later be used directly in any subsequent scenarios? (ex: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/7741)
